author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Large shareholder-return plans from Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are testing South Korea’s effort to narrow the longstanding valuation gap between its companies and global peers.

Reuters reported that the two chipmakers’ payout plans are worth more than 130 trillion won, about $97 billion, for 2026. Strong demand tied to artificial intelligence has boosted cash generation and increased investor pressure for dividends and share buybacks.

Investors welcomed the planned distributions but said broader changes in governance, capital allocation and shareholder rights are still needed. Samsung faces particular calls to put more emphasis on repurchasing shares rather than relying mainly on dividends.

At the time of the Reuters report, the benchmark KOSPI remained about 26% below the record it reached in June, even though Samsung and SK Hynix account for nearly half of the index’s weight. That percentage is a dated market measure, not a live quotation. The muted response illustrates why South Korea’s reform program will be judged across many companies and over time, not by two large payouts alone.
dek: The chipmakers’ combined 2026 shareholder-return plans exceed 130 trillion won, but investors say governance and capital-allocation concerns remain.
headline: Samsung and SK Hynix payouts test South Korea’s market reforms
